title: Reference images: CLIP vision, unCLIP and style models
hook: Two general doors in core for a picture. A style model adds tokens to the prompt. unCLIP changes the model's global vector. CLIP vision makes the numbers for both, and it isn't a model that generates anything.

verified.claim: CLIPVisionEncode returns an output with last_hidden_state, image_embeds and penultimate_hidden_states.
StyleModelApply concatenates the style model's output to the text tensor along tokens.
unCLIPConditioning adds to an unclip_conditioning list in the dict, and returns the input unchanged at strength 0.
load_style_model picks StyleAdapter or the Redux encoder from the file's keys.
Redux maps 1152 numbers per token to 4096.
The SD 2.1 unCLIP class and SDXL use the key, through unclip_adm and sdxl_pooled.
SDXLRefiner, StableCascade_C and Lumina2 also read unclip_conditioning, and core nodes for Wan and Hunyuan read a clip_vision_output directly.
The flux_redux render used core's StyleModelApply, with a pack's sampler, on FLUX.1 schnell.

unchecked: We didn't run c_unclip or c_style_redux. They pass validation only, and the model file names in them are examples.
The vision model's token counts in the lab are stand-ins. Real counts depend on the vision model.
We read the attn_bias path but don't claim what it does to a picture.
We describe the core nodes only. IP-Adapter is a separate paper and a third-party pack, and CU-214 covers the idea.
